root_cause.error: stage 0: AttributeError: 'PhaseAAuthorization' object has no attribute 'require_evidence'
root_cause.summary: ContinuationDriver never overrides PhaseADriver's AUTHORIZATION_TYPE / AUTHORIZATION_PATH class attributes, so on the pod it loaded logs/autoinit_phase_a_authorization.json as a PhaseAAuthorization — a real, committed file — instead of its own ContinuationAuthorization. stage_bind then called require_evidence(), which only ContinuationAuthorization has.
root_cause.the_seam_predicted_this: PhaseADriver's own comment on those attributes says: 'the continuation subclasses this driver: with the path fixed here, the continuation would have loaded attempt 12's CONSUMED Phase-A authorization on the pod ... Not a crash; a silently wrong ceiling, and evidence naming the wrong grant.' The seam was built for exactly this subclass and the subclass did not use it. It crashed rather than being silent only because require_evidence does not exist on the Phase-A type — a lucky failure mode.
root_cause.the_repair_is_not_one_line: setting the two attributes alone moves the failure to the NEXT statement: PhaseADriver.__init__ ends with self.auth.require_plan(PHASE_A_PLAN_V1.plan_hash), and a ContinuationAuthorization refuses it — verified at $0: 'this authorization binds plan a2ef4cd68a4b and the session runs 9377a2dc61f2'. The parent also stamps the Phase-A evidence schema and scope. PhaseBDriver solved the same problem by NOT calling super().__init__ and reimplementing it with its own TYPE, PATH and PLAN; ContinuationDriver calls super().__init__ and inherits all four wrong things.
root_cause.class: the fourth instance of inherited-contracts-not-needs, and the first to reach a driver stage. Attempt 1 was a missing input declaration; this is a missing seam override.

why_no_zero_cost_check_caught_it.the_whole_function_test_overwrites_the_e:
tests/pod/test_continuation_b_executes.py builds the driver with the REAL __init__ — which loaded the wrong authorization there too — and then immediately discards it:
    driver = ContinuationDriver.__new__(ContinuationDriver)
    ContinuationDriver.__init__(driver, Args())
    driver.auth = make_auth(...)   # <- overwrites
Every later assertion ran against a correctly-typed authorization the test supplied, so the seam's wrong default was loaded and masked in the same three lines. Seam injection points are the blind spot: extracting an injectable seam makes the injected value the only unexecuted code left.
why_no_zero_cost_check_caught_it.the_launcher_gate_asked_a_different_obje: evidence_binding_gate calls ContinuationDriver.observed_evidence() and then ctx.auth.require_evidence(observed) — where ctx.auth is the LAUNCHER's correctly-loaded ContinuationAuthorization. The gate proved the evidence matches the grant; it never exercised the DRIVER's own load path.
why_no_zero_cost_check_caught_it.how_to_close_it: assert the type and path the driver's real __init__ produces, before any test-supplied auth replaces it — and assert it for every PhaseADriver subclass, so a new one cannot inherit Phase A's grant silently.
